inputs.caption:
Global Metadata: Minimal Japanese art-pop, 96 BPM, A minor. A complete two-minute song with a full structure: short intro, verse, chorus, second verse, chorus, bridge, final chorus, brief outro. Wistful but quietly hopeful, late-night city rain mood.

Vocal Details: Soft androgynous Japanese lead vocal, close-mic and breathy, clear diction. Light harmony enters on the second chorus and stays through the final chorus. No spoken dialogue.

Arrangement: Warm felt piano, rounded bass, brushed electronic kick, soft rim-click snare, subtle tape hiss, one glassy synth line. Start with piano alone, bring in the beat under the first verse, open the harmony on each chorus, thin out to piano and voice for the bridge, return with the full arrangement for the final chorus, end on a gentle unresolved piano note.
inputs.lyrics:
[Intro]

[Verse 1]
Rain draws a map across the glass
Neon rivers slowly pass
I keep one small light awake
For the morning we will make

[Chorus]
Even in the blue hour, we begin again
Counting every streetlight till the long night ends
Hold the little warmth we found
Even in the blue hour, we begin again

[Verse 2]
Trains go quiet one by one
Puddles hold a borrowed sun
Every window tells a tale
Paper boats that learn to sail

[Chorus]
Even in the blue hour, we begin again
Counting every streetlight till the long night ends
Hold the little warmth we found
Even in the blue hour, we begin again

[Bridge]
If the city never sleeps
I will keep the time you keep
Soft as rain on silver wire
One small spark, one small fire

[Final Chorus]
Even in the blue hour, we begin again
Counting every streetlight till the long night ends
Hold the little warmth we found
Even in the blue hour, we begin again

[Outro]
We begin again
